client_to_server.shape: { type: 'input', data: string }  — raw PTY stdin bytes (UTF-8 encoded). Multiple WS clients can all write concurrently; the backend serializes writes with a mutex to prevent byte-level corruption (single-user assumption — semantic collisions are the user's problem).
{ type: 'resize', cols: u16, rows: u16 }  — applied immediately via TIOCSWINSZ. Last writer wins when multiple clients disagree on dimensions.
{ type: 'init' }  — no-op (legacy from v1 handshake); safely ignored.

server_to_client.shape: Raw PTY output bytes, byte-identical to what the shell produced. Feed directly into the terminal parser (SwiftTerm / xterm.js). No prefix; no encoding transformation; may contain ANSI escapes, multi-byte UTF-8 split across frames, alt-screen sequences.
First two bytes `\x00\x01` then ASCII string `CTL:<name>`. Control-plane signals — never contain PTY output. Recognized markers: `replay_start`, `replay_done`, `session_ended`, `subscriber_lagged`.

markers.replay_start: Sent once per attach, immediately after upgrade. Indicates the following Binary frames are replay bytes from the persistent log (conversation scrollback). Client MAY show a loading indicator.
markers.replay_done: Sent once after all replay bytes have been streamed. All subsequent Binary frames are live PTY output. Client SHOULD hide any loading indicator.
markers.session_ended: Sent when the PTY process has exited (shell exit, DELETE conversation, fatal log write error). The WebSocket closes with a normal close frame after this marker. Client SHOULD dismiss the terminal UI and mark the conversation as ended locally.
markers.subscriber_lagged: Sent when the internal broadcast channel overflows for this client (client fell too far behind the live stream). The WebSocket closes immediately after. Client SHOULD reconnect — the next attach will replay any bytes missed.

ws_protocol.keepalive: server sends Ping every 30s; client must Pong within 90s or the connection is dropped

v2_semantics: One PTY per conversation. Sessions survive WS disconnect, app close, network drops, device suspend. The only ways a PTY dies are: (a) shell exits normally, (b) DELETE conversation, (c) backend restart (zero state), (d) fatal log write error.

Multiple concurrent WebSockets on the same conversation are allowed — all receive the same replay + live stream. There is no 'commander' concept and no close code 4000. Two iOS devices + the macOS app can all attach simultaneously.

Replay is **complete** — the full byte history from conversation creation is streamed on every attach. The server persists every PTY byte to an append-only log file (0600, under `$THEYOS_CONVERSATIONS_DIR`). There is no cap, no ring buffer, no truncation.
reattach_flow_example: ← Binary <raw bytes 0..N of scrollback, in one or more frames>
… live Binary frames interleaved with client Text input …
breaking_changes_vs_v1: Output moved from Text frames to raw Binary. v1 Text chunks would corrupt multi-byte UTF-8 at frame boundaries (U+FFFD substitution); v2 is byte-perfect.
`pane_size:{w}x{h}`, `resync_start`, `resync_done`, `resize_applied` markers removed — no tmux means no equivalent server-side state to re-sync against.
Close code 4000 (`commander_changed`) removed. Clients that still listen for it will never see it.
`client=mobile` query param removed (was a tmux-specific hint).

`/session-info` endpoint removed. Commander role no longer exists; clients don't need to pre-check who owns a session before attaching.
`/tmux/windows` endpoint removed. No tmux in v2.
`/tmux/panes` endpoint removed. No tmux in v2.
`/tmux/cwd` endpoint removed. CWD can be derived from shell output if the app needs it.
`/tmux/pane-stream` endpoint removed. Peek/pop flows should use `terminal_pty_ws` (multi-attach now works).
`/tmux/capture-pane` endpoint removed. The replay from `terminal_pty_ws` provides equivalent (and better) scrollback access.
